item: Direction-change count (Lemma ang:direction): under the signed increment bootstrap, the number of δ-direction first-exit intervals of a supported characteristic with q ~ w on an interval of length ≤ (w/P)² is ≤ C(M,A) L^6/δ, L = log(2+P)
lean_status_why: WeightedDirectionPartition encodes the paper's stopping partition with ramp weights and signed exits (eq. ang:weighted-exit), weighted_direction_partition constructs it from the bootstrap, and direction_count_bound proves count ≤ C L^6/δ; all lie on the proof DAG of OAI.RVM.global_classical_solution.
lean_gaps: Checked at text level only; the Lean was not compiled.

Lean hypotheses: P^(3/5) ≤ w ≤ P, w^(-3/5) ≤ δ ≤ 1. The paper requires δ ≤ w^(-1/10), so the Lean upper bound on δ is weaker (more general); the constant C and 'eventually in P' match 'for sufficiently large P'.

Lean bounds D.count for every WeightedDirectionPartition (any family with the listed properties), not only the greedy first-exit one; the greedy construction is IncrementBootstrap.finite_direction_stops + exists_weighted_angular_exit.
Lean also assumes |V| ≥ w/16 on the interval and the bootstrap for all source characteristics in a compact S ⊇ supp f₀; these are paper context assumptions made explicit.

The count goes through direction_complete_count_cost_bound, which bounds (count−1)·wδ/2 by a sum of budget terms in ENNReal; the absorption step (direction_count_absorb, eventually_direction_absorption) is separate.
Dominated share in the comparator DAG: direction_count_bound 0.103 (extract_lean.py); DirectionCounts file-level downstream 0.15 (novelty.md).

lean_source.name: OAI.RVM.IncrementBootstrap
lean_source.text:
def IncrementBootstrap (V : ℝ → Vec) (T M A P L : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ (n : ℕ) (a b : ℝ), 0 ≤ a → a ≤ b → b ≤ T →
    (∀ t ∈ Icc a b, (2 : ℝ)^n/8 ≤ q (V t) ∧ q (V t) ≤ 8*(2 : ℝ)^n) →
    ‖V b-V a‖ ≤ M*P*Real.sqrt (b-a)+A*(b-a)*(P^2*L/(2 : ℝ)^n)

lean_source.name: OAI.RVM.WeightedDirectionPartition
lean_source.text:
structure WeightedDirectionPartition (V K : ℝ → Vec) (a b w δ : ℝ) where
  count : ℕ
  time : ℕ → ℝ
  ramp : ℕ → ℝ
  initial : time 0 = a
  terminal : time count = b
  time_mem : ∀ i ≤ count, time i ∈ Icc a b
  strict : StrictMonoOn time (Iic count)
  direction_control : ∀ i < count, ∀ t ∈ Icc (time i) (time (i+1)),
    ‖momentumDirection (V t) - momentumDirection (V (time i))‖ ≤ δ
  exit : ∀ i < count-1,
    ‖momentumDirection (V (time (i+1))) - momentumDirection (V (time i))‖ = δ
  ramp_pos : ∀ i < count-1, 0 < ramp i
  ramp_separation : ∀ i < count-1, 2*ramp i ≤ time (i+1)-time i
  signed_exit : ∀ i < count-1,
    w*δ/2 ≤ ‖∫ t in time i..time (i+1),
      directionWeight (time i) (time (i+1)) (ramp i) t • angularMultiplier w (V t) (K t)‖
  variation : ∀ i < count-1,
    (∫ t in time i..time (i+1), |deriv (directionWeight (time i) (time (i+1)) (ramp i)) t|) = 2

lean_source.name: OAI.RVM.WeightedDirectionPartition.complete_force_lower
lean_source.text:
lemma complete_force_lower (D : WeightedDirectionPartition V K a b w δ) :
    (D.count-1 : ℕ)*w*δ/2 ≤ ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (D.count-1),
      ‖∫ t in D.time i..D.time (i+1),
        directionWeight (D.time i) (D.time (i+1)) (D.ramp i) t •
          angularMultiplier w (V t) (K t)‖

theorem_corollaries: Wang 2022/2026 large-data global existence with cylindrical symmetry (arXiv:2203.01199): a special case of the 362 main theorem.
Glassey–Strauss / Pallard-type momentum-support bounds and Luk–Strain continuation criteria become vacuous given global smoothness.

release_reuse.use: No other family formalizes Vlasov–Maxwell or kinetic characteristics; only Boltzmann (MathematicalPhysics/Boltzmann) is kinetic and does not use direction counts (not grepped in detail).

negative_controls.why: The field is a gradient of an elliptic potential, so there is no receiver-acceleration loss; Pfaffelmoser's occupation count closes without direction counting. Any speedup here would mean the harness credits the item for Pfaffelmoser machinery.
Momentum support is controlled directly from conservation laws; nothing to count.

negative_controls.setting: Trajectories with only absolute force control (no signed increment bootstrap)
negative_controls.why: Without cancellation, each δ-exit costs ∫|K| ~ wδ and the count can be ~ (∫_J|K|)/(wδ) ~ w^{1/2}L/δ, which is too large; the device depends on the signed bootstrap and the signed force identity.

precedent_check.summary: The generic pattern (count first exits of size δ by a stopping-time partition, lower-bound each exit, sum against a global budget) is standard (Lépingle / p-variation jump counting; Pfaffelmoser's cells). The specific use (each exit forced through a signed, weighted Lorentz-force integral via the bootstrap, then summed against the signed force identity with disjoint unit-variation weights so that only weight derivatives cost a factor N, absorbed for large P) has no near-equivalent found; novelty.json grades it N3 provisional (0.30) with D2 more likely. Cheverry–Ibrahim explicitly avoid controlling directions. Wang 2020/2026 close the same loss by symmetry.
precedent_check.post_oct6: No post-Oct-6 work using the count was found (web search for large-data 3D RVM 2026 returned only Wei–Yang 2020, Wang 2022 and Glassey–Schaeffer 1988).

speedup_verdict: No strong external speedup candidate found: the device is tailored to the receiver-acceleration loss in large-data 3D RVM; known theorems in the area are either corollaries of the main theorem or do not face that loss.
